# Framework API

## Purpose

The Operational Topology Framework exposes stable source-level entry points for
building axial operational worlds without importing the demonstration
application.

The extraction separates five responsibilities:

```txt
framework core
browser integration
lab and animation fixtures
scene presets and templates
application configuration and content
```

The framework is reusable inside and outside this repository. It is published
on npm with core, browser, labs, and presets entry points. The API follows a
`0.x` semantic-versioning policy while external usage continues to shape the
public boundary.

## Entry Points

### Core

```ts
import {
  createOperationalTopology,
  type OperationalTopologyDefinition,
} from "../src/framework/index.ts";
```

`src/framework/index.ts` exports:

- axial geometry and grid generation
- topology and world models
- camera math
- connector contracts
- signal engine, policy, and coordinator
- relationship context
- render-frame and SVG renderer contracts
- knowledge repository
- reusable scene configuration defaults
- reusable scene presets and template contracts
- presentation slide definitions and topology generation
- semantic theme contracts
- the `createOperationalTopology()` composition factory

The core entry focuses on environment-neutral topology construction. Portfolio
records, page profiles, browser event controllers, Developer API registration,
and lab animations belong to their scoped entry points.

### Browser

```ts
import {
  createTopologyContentPageController,
  createSceneNavigationController,
} from "../src/framework/browser.ts";
```

`src/framework/browser.ts` owns DOM and interaction integration:

- selection events
- page navigation orchestration
- viewport and scene navigation controllers
- content-page controller
- same-SVG dataset transitions for replacing one topology with another
- development registration and `window.otf` support

Consumers that only need geometry, normalization, rendering preparation, or
server-side world construction should not import this entry. Browser consumers
that render an interactive scene should use this entry for DOM-bound controllers
and dataset transitions.

Dataset transitions use the existing scene SVG and preserve the canonical grid.
They are intentionally browser-scoped because they operate on live SVG DOM:

```ts
import {
  createTopologyDatasetTransition,
} from "operational-topology/browser";

const transition = createTopologyDatasetTransition({
  sceneGrid,
  cells,
  radius: 28,
  connectorRouting: "straight",
});

await transition.transition({
  nodes,
  relationships,
});
```

The consumer owns dataset creation and Inspector updates. The transition
controller owns staging, ordered reveal, cancellation, and swapping the active
content layer without creating a second scene.

### Labs

```ts
import {
  getCenterBloomFrame,
  getGhLogoFrame,
} from "../src/framework/labs.ts";
```

`src/framework/labs.ts` contains optional demonstrations and experimental
animation presets. These modules are not required by the core renderer.

### Presets

```ts
import {
  TOPOLOGY_SCENE_PRESETS,
  createTopologyScenePreset,
} from "../src/framework/presets.ts";
```

`src/framework/presets.ts` contains reusable scene presets and template
definitions for application shells, intro scenes, main site scenes, and page
families that share camera, minimap, and signal defaults.

Labs support experiments, demos, and animation testing. Presets provide
reusable templates that production pages can compose.

Presets should be exportable without dragging in animation-only fixtures.

### Presentations

Presentation data can be defined independently from the page that renders it:

```ts
import {
  createPresentationDeck,
  createPresentationSlides,
} from "operational-topology";

const deck = createPresentationDeck({
  id: "architecture-deck",
  title: "Architecture Deck",
  defaultSlideId: "architecture",
  sceneLayout: "world-grid",
  topologyLayout: "ring",
  slides: [
    {
      id: "architecture",
      title: "System Architecture",
      subtitle: "Services and dependencies",
      summary: "A presentation slide with an interactive topology.",
      status: "ready",
      route: "/system-architecture",
      role: "architecture",
      anchors: [
        {
          id: "edge",
          label: "Edge",
          children: [{ id: "gateway", label: "Gateway" }],
        },
        {
          id: "application",
          label: "Application",
          children: [
            { id: "api", label: "API" },
            { id: "services", label: "Services" },
          ],
        },
        {
          id: "data",
          label: "Data",
          children: [{ id: "database", label: "Database" }],
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
});

const slides = createPresentationSlides(deck);
```

Each slide contains a reusable `TopologyDataset` and Inspector records. A
presentation page can pass the datasets to
`createTopologyDatasetTransition()` and control the sequence independently.

The current topology layouts are:

- `ring` - root-centered radial topology for contextual maps
- `linear` - left-to-right anchor chain with vertically aligned child branches
- `fishspine` - left-to-right anchor chain with alternating upper and lower child branches
- `radial-sectors` - centered layout with exclusive domain sectors

Scene layouts:

- `viewport-fit` - fit the operational world to the viewport
- `world-grid` - render the world over a larger grid-backed scene

Astro applications can author slide definitions in a Markdown collection and
map the validated frontmatter to `PresentationSlideDefinition`. The sample
application uses `src/content/presentations/` for this purpose. The collection
owns authored titles, summaries, routes, roles, anchors, and child labels;
rendering and transition behavior remain framework responsibilities.

## Composition Factory

`createOperationalTopology()` creates one coherent runtime from a declarative
definition.

```ts
import { createOperationalTopology } from "../src/framework/index.ts";

const topology = createOperationalTopology({
  grid: {
    radius: 28,
    columns: 12,
    rows: 10,
    originQ: -6,
    originR: -5,
  },
  entities: [
    {
      id: "root",
      label: "Root",
      q: 0,
      r: 0,
      variant: "root",
    },
    {
      id: "journal",
      label: "Journal",
      q: 3,
      r: 2,
      variant: "anchor",
    },
  ],
  relationships: [
    {
      from: "root",
      to: "journal",
      kind: "parent",
    },
  ],
  signal: {
    transitionSpeed: 1.35,
  },
});
```

The returned runtime exposes:

```ts
topology.model
topology.world
topology.repository
topology.signalPolicy
topology.getEntity(id)
topology.getRelationshipContext(id)
topology.createRenderFrame(options)
```

This keeps geometry, normalized knowledge, semantic relationships, signals, and
render preparation aligned around the same definition.

## Definition Validation

The factory rejects:

- non-positive radius
- non-positive or non-integer rows and columns
- duplicate entity identifiers
- relationships that reference missing entities

Definitions may be checked without creating a runtime:

```ts
const issues = inspectOperationalTopologyDefinition(definition);
```

Validation is intentionally structural. Domain-specific content validation
remains the responsibility of the application or its content collection schema.

## Application Boundary

Application-owned modules remain outside the public core:

```txt
src/config/topologyPageProfiles.ts
src/topology/siteKnowledge.ts
src/topology/worldMapRecords.ts
src/content/
src/pages/
```

Page profiles may compose reusable framework defaults, but the framework does
not know about `home`, `lab`, `worldMap`, personal records, or demonstration
routes.

## Compatibility

`src/topology/index.ts` remains as a backward-compatible aggregate for existing
code. New code should use one of the scoped framework entry points so its runtime
and dependency requirements are explicit.

Astro components now consume the public core entry for shared model and geometry
contracts. Existing implementation modules remain in `src/topology/` to avoid a
high-risk physical move while the API boundary stabilizes.

## Package Readiness

The package has published core, browser, labs, and presets entry points. The
browser entry now includes the dataset transition contract, so external browser
consumers can use the same scene-swapping capability as the application.

Remaining release work is limited to normal API evolution:

- keep browser and core entry-point exports covered by boundary tests
- exercise new contracts in an external consumer fixture
- preserve the documented semantic-versioning policy for future releases

Framework extraction does not require changing canonical axial coordinates,
world behavior, or renderer semantics.
